title: Black Kite Introduces Quantum Readiness Controls to Assess Third-Party Cryptographic Risk - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Black Kite added a Quantum Readiness control set to the SSL/TLS Strength category of its Cyber Rating engine to externally assess vendors' post-quantum cryptography posture. The article ties it to US OMB M-26-15 (key establishment by 2030, signatures by 2031), Executive Order 14412 and EU NIS2 supply-chain mandates.

insights.claim: Black Kite launched Quantum Readiness, a control set within the SSL/TLS Strength category of its Cyber Rating engine, to evaluate post-quantum cryptographic agility across third-party vendor supply chains.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: PQC assessment is being productized into existing third-party risk tools.
insights.locator: Third-party cyber risk management platform provider Black Kite

insights.claim: The tool gives external visibility into which vendors use hybrid post-quantum key exchange and PQC certificate signature readiness versus legacy RSA, ECDSA and ECDH algorithms facing phase-out.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Outside-in scanning offers a scalable proxy for vendor quantum risk.

insights.claim: OMB M-26-15 mandates post-quantum key establishment by 2030 and digital signatures by 2031, Executive Order 14412 sets contractor migration targets, and EU NIS2 imposes supply chain cryptographic mandates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hard compliance dates create dated demand for PQC tooling and services.
insights.locator: The rollout addresses mounting regulatory compliance deadlines

insights.claim: The article lists a NIST deprecation schedule for legacy algorithms after 2030 and complete disallowance in 2035.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 2035 disallowance date bounds the migration window for enterprise vendors.

insights.claim: By continuously observing vendors' external cryptographic signals, Black Kite aims to help enterprises and government agencies mitigate harvest now, decrypt later vulnerabilities before mandatory national PQC migration deadlines.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Data stolen today can be decrypted later, so vendor exposure matters before quantum computers arrive.
